setlist.title: Untitled (I Might Compare) - this is a lyric from the Sweden era which JD dug up for that silent film score he did in 2010. other than that this is the only other recording of it I'm aware of. we still don't know its real title, if it had one
Birthday Song (This TIme Has Gone) - unreleased track played from the mid 90s to 2000ish mostly
My Favorite Things - probably the most well-known song on here, which is a wild thing to say. it's on a lot of bootlegs. I love John Coltrane!

Pure Change - that's what JD introduces it as but I always knew it as Pure Sun because of the one other recording. Song played once in like 1994 and then sometime last decade there was a show where he tried to remember it and only got through the first verse
Real Good Girlfriend - very cute song played once in Belgium about a month after this and then as far as I know never again. this recording is so amazing, gotta be my highlight
Are Friends Electric? (Gary Numan cover, two takes)

liner.body_md: This rare 1996 radio session captures the Mountain Goats performing for FSK in Hamburg, Germany, during their tour with Cakekitchen [1]. The lineup features JD on guitar and vocals, accompanied by Graeme Jefferies on piano, Markus Acher on percussion, and Peter Hughes on bass [1]. Taped by Gregor Kessler and transferred by notasfarwest, this twenty-four-minute recording is the only known archive of the show [1]. It includes five legendary tracks that have no other archived performances, such as the untitled song from the Sweden era and the unreleased “Birthday Song” [1]. The set also features “My Favorite Things,” a well-known track with thirteen other archived performances, and “Pure Change,” which the band introduced by that name [1]. The performance highlights include “Real Good Girlfriend,” described as a very cute song that was rarely played, and a two-take cover of Gary Numan’s “Are Friends Electric?” [1]. This session offers a unique glimpse into the band's mid-nineties repertoire, preserving songs that are otherwise difficult to find [1].
